title: Functions: Definition and Basic Usage
objectives: Define functions using def with parameters
Use functions to avoid code duplication

content.title: What is a Function?
content.explanation: A function is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task. You define it once with def, then call it by name whenever needed. Functions help organize code, avoid repetition, and make programs easier to understand.

content.title: Parameters vs Arguments
content.explanation: Parameters are variables in the function definition. Arguments are the actual values passed when calling. They are matched by position by default.
key_points: Inside function, parameters act like local variables

content.title: Multiple Parameters
content.explanation: Functions can have multiple parameters. Default values make parameters optional.

content.title: Return Values
content.explanation: The return statement sends a value back to the caller. Functions without return implicitly return None. Return exits the function immediately.

content.title: Return Examples
content.explanation: Return can be used for computed values or early exit from loops.

exercises.title: Create a Function
exercises.description: Write a function square(n) that returns n squared. Test it with 3, 5, 10.
exercises.solution:
def square(n):
    return n * n

print(square(3))   # 9
print(square(5))   # 25
print(square(10))  # 100

exercises.title: Multiple Parameters
exercises.description: Write a function rectangle_area(width, height) that returns the area. Test with different values.
exercises.solution:
def rectangle_area(width, height):
    return width * height

print(rectangle_area(3, 4))   # 12
print(rectangle_area(5, 10))  # 50

quiz.question: What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?
options: Parameter in definition, argument in call
Argument in definition, parameter in call
Parameter is required, argument is optional
quiz.correct_answer: Parameter in definition, argument in call
quiz.explanation: Parameters are placeholders in the function definition. Arguments are actual values passed when calling.
